text:
adele: Heads up — after the fused-attn-v3 kernel flip last night we started getting a cluster of OOMs on the p4d pools. Noticed sustained pad growth in continuous batching accounting, esp for seq_len 1024+ :frowning:

marty: which pools and which job classes?

adele: prod-p4d-a and prod-p4d-b, mostly long-context chat routes (route: chat/long). KV cache prefill bytes are +12% vs baseline.

lin: did the batching heuristic change too? I remember a PR touching greedy grouping.

adele: yes — PR #4921 switched prefer_grouping=true to favor throughput (batches group more aggressively). The combination looks like it's increasing per-batch padding because groups contain wider length variance.

samir: can you drop the profiler snapshot / nvidia-smi?

adele: pasted a short extract:
```
GPU 0  PID 12345  Mem used 25.4G / 40G
...workspace_peak: 6.2G
Batcher: avg batch_size 8 -> avg padded_tokens +25%
KV cache: prefill_bytes 1.12x baseline
```

adele: and a perf flame (internal link): https://perf.redwood/fg/1894012345 (shows new kernel carving a temp buffer per-head) :eyes:

marty: hypothesis: fused-attn-v3 reduced compute by ~6% but trades that for a larger transient workspace per invocation. Combined with bigger groups you get more simultaneous transient buffers -> accounting shows pad growth and allocator pressure.

lin: if that's true we should see per-seq overhead scale with batch_size not token_count. Do the traces show per-call temp allocations?

adele: yes — kernel allocs are sized by (heads * head_dim * temp_multiplier). For long contexts that multiplier grows.

tara: interesting — allocator config currently has workspace_reserve=0.12 and slab_coalesce=true. Might be worth toggling reserve and enabling more aggressive buffer reuse instead of new temp allocations.

samir: short-term mitigation: revert batching heuristic OR revert kernel. Which is quicker?

lin: revert heuristic is a config flip (minutes). Kernel rollback touches model runtime and perf suites (hrs).

adele: I started a canary revert of prefer_grouping on prod-p4d-a 10m ago; memory pressure dropped ~18% in the canary window.

marty: great. For the medium term we should:
- add kernel-level hinting to allow fused-attn-v3 to use preallocated shared workspace when available
- add accounting metric for "transient_workspace_per_call" to the runtime telemetry
- update batching heuristic to incorporate transient_workspace estimate per model variant when grouping decisions are made

lin: agree. Also add an allocator knob: prefer_reuse_over_new so slab allocator will try to fit temps into existing workspaces instead of creating new ones (fall back still allowed).

adele: filed tasks: INF-1184 (telemetry), INF-1185 (allocator knob), INF-1186 (kernel hint API).

sre-bot: incident created INC-2026 (padding-growth OOMs) — paging thresholds set.

deploy-bot: canary rollback completed on prod-p4d-a at 1894012600. No regressions observed.

marty: next steps for owners:
- adele: confirm KV cache prefill didn't change semantics (just timing)
- lin: prototype prefer_reuse_over_new on allocator (small patch)
- samir: schedule kernel follow-up with perf team to add shared-workspace path

adele: acked, will validate KV prefill.

samir: I'll coordinate with perf. If folks agree we can roll the heuristic revert to prod-p4d-b after another canary.

tara: filing a doc note for the ops runbook: "if padding spike occurs after kernel/heuristic change -> consider heuristic revert first, then allocator patches, then kernel rollback".

marty: thanks everyone. We'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
